calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all affected crossings
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected with visible focus. The answer lists the riverside path closing, the ferry stopping, and the footbridge closing. Captures: A-1440-before and A-1440-after.

A-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; A-1440-edge shows only the path in the answer. Its two amber end bars are visible at the lower-left and upper-right ends of the curved bank-side path. The open footbridge is continuous; the open ferry has a dotted connection between banks. The path itself remains continuous, so its end bars carry the closure cue.
A-1440.fact_check: The rendered answer supports the requested path-only result at 2 m and the three affected crossings at 6 m. At 6 m the ferry is docked and its connection is interrupted, but the picture alone does not make a stopped ferry unmistakable; the answer text supplies that meaning. Real-world thresholds were not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The large river illustration makes the three locations easy to associate with their labels.
A-1440.weakness: The closed path retains a bright continuous line, and the stopped ferry is visually subtle.
A-1440.repair: Show an unmistakable interruption or obstruction on the closed path and a clearer stationary ferry state.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all affected crossings
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected and the answer listed the path, ferry, and footbridge. Controls, map, and answer fit in the 390 by 844 viewport. Captures: A-390-before and A-390-after.

A-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; A-390-edge shows only the path in the answer. Both path end bars remain visible: one near the left edge and one above the bend. The open bridge is continuous and the ferry connection is dotted; the closed path also remains continuous between its small end bars.
A-390.fact_check: The on-screen answer supports path-only closure at 2 m. The 6 m answer says the ferry stops, but the small docked boat and interrupted route do not independently make that state unmistakable. Real-world thresholds were not independently verified.
A-390.strength: The entire task fits on screen with a clear keyboard focus outline.
A-390.weakness: The small closure markers are easy to miss, especially the left path endpoint.
A-390.repair: Make the endpoint barriers and closed route geometry more legible at phone size.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all affected crossings
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected with visible focus. The answer lists the path closing, ferry stopping, and footbridge closing; the map labels them Closed, Stopped, and Closed. Captures: B-1440-before and B-1440-after.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; B-1440-edge shows the path closed and the footbridge and ferry open. Both path endpoints are visible as amber bars at the lower-left and upper-right ends of the curved bank-side route. The bridge is continuous and the ferry has a dotted crossing; the closed path remains continuous between its end bars.
B-1440.fact_check: The answer and map labels agree on the path-only result at 2 m and the three affected crossings at 6 m. The docked boat and broken connection suggest a stopped ferry, but the imagery alone is ambiguous; the Stopped label makes the stated status explicit. Real-world thresholds were not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: Route-specific status labels let residents read the state directly beside each crossing.
B-1440.weakness: The closed path's continuous line and small barriers still require interpretation; the ferry relies on its status label for certainty.
B-1440.repair: Strengthen the physical interruption at both path ends and make the ferry's stopped state recognizable without text or color.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all affected crossings
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected and the path, ferry, and footbridge were all listed and labeled with their states. Controls, illustration, and answer fit in the 390 by 844 viewport. Captures: B-390-before and B-390-after.

B-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; B-390-edge shows only the path closed, with the footbridge and ferry labeled open. Both path end bars are visible: the lower-left bar lies close to the screen edge and the upper-right bar sits above the bend. The open bridge is continuous and the ferry route dotted, while the closed path remains a continuous curve between small barriers.
B-390.fact_check: The visible answer and labels support the path-only result. At 6 m, the stopped label is clear, but the small boat and interrupted ferry connection alone do not make its stopped state unmistakable. Real-world thresholds were not independently verified.
B-390.strength: The local status labels and full answer remain visible alongside the controls.
B-390.weakness: Small route geometry and barriers make the visual distinction depend heavily on labels and color.
B-390.repair: Enlarge or redraw the barriers and interrupted ferry route so their states remain recognizable at phone scale without relying on labels, animation, or color.

preference.reason: B preserves the clear keyboard interaction and compact layout while placing explicit status beside each crossing. Both designs need stronger visual route-state cues, especially for the stopped ferry and the continuous-looking closed path.
